> A desk display that shows what's playing on my Mac: album art, song title, artist, a live progress bar, and a play/pause indicator on a 2.8" colour screen. Spotify's API now requires Premium for developers, and I don't have it. So I plan to use a Python script on my MacBook reads the Spotify web player, resizes the cover art, and sends it over my home WiFi to an ESP32 display board that draws it in real time. No API keys and no subscription needed. What makes it mine is the Mac-to-ESP32 pipeline I wrote and also the homemade case for the harder using  cardboard .

## Design

### 2026-10-01 — I brainstormed and planned my project, a desk display that shows what's playing on my Mac.

**1h**

I brainstormed and planned my project, a desk display that shows what's playing on my Mac.

What I did:

Came up with the idea: a small screen that shows the album cover, song title, and artist of the current song.
Thought about how it would work.

Listed the features I want: album art, title and artist, a progress bar, and a play/pause icon.

I also created some AI images of how the thing would look like

Wrote down rough ideas for the parts and a simple case.

### 2026-10-01 — I settled on the design of the project and chose the parts.

**2.5h**

I settled on the design of the project and chose the parts.

What I did:

Picked the exact parts: an ESP32 board with a built-in screen and a USB-C data cable.

![Image3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/psEhAcze3X3bWLEMFSmxYAEC5kfNzh6A/8df1154ba612fc3f57927cca11645d5a1cc19f28e78291ce91f7f65c3c14f8fc.png)
Dropped the e-ink display idea, because it refreshes slowly and would lag when songs change or the progress bar updates. Instead  a normal colour screen can update in real time.

Decided to build the case from home materials (cardboard, plastic, paint) instead of paying for a 3D printing service, to stay within budget of$30.

I also ran into a major problem as Spotify's API needs a Premium account, which I don't have. So I asked Claude for help and learned that I can use a Python script on my Mac to read the song info  such as the title, artist, cover art and play state directly from the Spotify desktop app.

### 2026-10-02 — Planned how the Mac and ESP32 will communicate over Wi-Fi. The Mac runs a small server, and the ESP32 checks it for the current song and sends playback commands.

**5h**

Planned how the Mac and ESP32 will communicate over Wi-Fi. The Mac runs a small server, and the ESP32 checks it for the current song and sends playback commands.

Set up the Python project and changed from reading Spotify directly to using `nowplaying-cli`, which works with Spotify in a browser and other website audio.

Created code to get the song title, artist, album cover, play state and progress. This process took hours of troubleshooting and testing. Some of the main challenges included improving the quality of the album cover and fixing the progress bar and timing.

I further designed a 320×240 screen layout with the album cover, song information, progress bar, time and playback buttons. The screen is used sideways (320 wide, 240 tall). The top half has the 80×80 cover on the left (25% of the width), with the bold song title and the artist next to it. The bottom half has the progress bar with the times, then the back, play/pause, and next buttons.

Split the project into separate files for music data, covers, screen drawing and the server, with `main.py` running everything. I then built and tested the local Mac server using my phone over Wi-Fi.

Other features I added include play/pause, next and previous controls, which I tested using `curl` commands. The server also has an access key so other devices on the Wi-Fi cannot control my music without permission.

### 2026-10-03 — Ran a final test of the whole Mac setup: starting mid-song, pausing, skipping, stopping playback, the access key, and the playback commands.

**3h**

Ran a final test of the whole Mac setup: starting mid-song, pausing, skipping, stopping playback, the access key, and the playback commands.

Cleaned up the project. I deleted old test files and the scripts that were replaced, and kept five working Python files. I also added a .gitignore so my access key and future WiFi password don't get uploaded, plus an example config file so other people know what to fill in.

Put the project on GitHub with a README that explains what it does, how it works, how to set it up.

First draft of the ESP32 code and put it in a firmware/ folder. It connects to WiFi, gets the song info from my Mac, downloads the cover, and draws the screen with the same layout as my preview. This code is not reliable yet. I can't test it until the board arrives, and some parts are guesses (like the backlight pin).

Decided to make the case after the board arrives, so it can be cut to fit the real measurements. I'll design it properly then.
